section.title: Applying EPB manually
section.p: Make sure the brake warning light () illuminates. If AUTO HOLD is active when the vehicle is turned off, EPB is applied automatically. The EPB is also applied if the EPB switch is pulled up after the vehicle is turned off. Do not operate the EPB while driving, except in emergency situations.

li.p: If the vehicle does not remain stationary on a steep incline or while pulling a trailer, follow the steps below:
Pull up the EPB switch and hold it for more than 3 seconds.
A clicking sound or electric brake motor whine may be heard when applying or releasing the EPB. This is normal and indicates proper system operation.

section.title: Applying EPB automatically
section.p: The Electronic Parking Brake (EPB) is applied automatically under the following conditions:

li.p: The EPB may automatically provide additional braking force after being applied for safety.
The driver turns off the vehicle while AUTO HOLD is active.
When the vehicle is shifted to P (Park).
The EPB is requested by other systems.

note.p: For vehicles equipped with EPB and AUTO HOLD:

li.p: If the vehicle is turned off while AUTO HOLD is active, the EPB will engage automatically.
To prevent this, turn off AUTO HOLD before turning off the vehicle.

section.title: Emergency braking
section.p: If there is a problem with the brake pedal while driving, emergency braking is possible by pulling up and holding the EPB switch. Braking is possible only while you are holding the EPB switch. However, braking distance will be longer than normal.

note.p: Do not operate EPB while the vehicle is moving except in an emergency situation. Applying the EPB while the vehicle is moving at normal speeds can cause a sudden loss of control of the vehicle. If you must use the EPB to stop the vehicle, use great caution in applying the brake.

li.p: During emergency braking by the EPB, the parking brake warning light will appear to indicate that the system is operating.

If you notice a continuous noise or burning smell when the EPB is used for emergency braking, have your vehicle inspected by a professional workshop. Kia recommends visiting an authorized Kia dealer or service partner.
